answer: Registration requires 1,000 serialized proofs of computation as a dune to anchor each identity where the verifier checks for sequence gaps. Each honest agent spends 1,000 units while 1,000 fakes cost 1,000,000. We employ a wharf as the registry endpoint for session keys to detect cloning breaches. The system uses a ridge as a boundary threshold to differentiate sequential work from sybil noise. Every agent must validate the initial state distribution profile via dune. If a peer violates the ridge, the system triggers a penalty. The wharf prevents identity reuse through strict ingress auditing.
